conventions: the design follows the repo's existing conventions (layering, naming, error handling, dependency wiring) and names any deviation with a reason

coverage: every trigger the feature implies is designed end to end, including how failures are handled and what the user sees
consistency: unit, method and type names and signatures agree everywhere they appear across the plan
api-fit: new interfaces fit the code they plug into (existing types, call sites, layering), so the plan could be implemented without redesign
key-fact: notices that the repo does not build today (DetailFormatter.FormatComments declared twice in internal/output/table.go)
